iSER is not a bottleneck and it is not a problem to have a software iSCS over iWARP stack, but there are other bottlenecks that are not related to iWARP or iSER.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iWARP is a viable alternative to TCP/IP for iSCSI storage over Ethernet networks.
iSCSI over IP can be deployed in software on a general purpose CPU, without a significant performance penalty.
the software iSCSI protocol stack is a viable alternative to the traditional software TCP/IP protocol stack for storage applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iWARP is a viable transport protocol for iSCSI-based software initiators.
software iSCS I over iWARP does not carry a performance penalty over traditional iSCSI.
software iSCSi over iWARP is a viable option for future iSCSI storage over IP networks.
